svg.text: Na/V ratio is the primary predictor
Results 1 and 2 both hit Na/V ≈ 10% and deliver 75–84% net speedup despite very different absolute sizes.
Result 3 at Na/V = 6% collapses net gains to 9%. The threshold appears to be around Na/V ≥ 8–10%.
Scale amplifies advantage — not diminishes it
R2 (V=300, Na=30) beats R1 (V=150, Na=15) by 9% net. Larger graphs have more redundant traversal for BFS to waste,
so MAFS's elimination of that redundancy becomes proportionally more valuable at scale.
Small graphs + few agents: fusion overhead dominates
R3: 42.7% gross collapses to 9% net — the O(V) memory union cost consumes most of the savings from only 3 agents.
